creativity.reason: Level 0: the business description covers observability, security and AI operations software and shows no creative activity. Office layouts that 'support creativity' are general language, and 'design' refers to engineering.

community.reason: Level 2: the only qualifying activities are employee development (leadership programs, global mentoring, career frameworks), so the Community cap of 2 applies.

cross_cultural.reason: Level 2: several specific current internal practices. These are seven named ERGs (no membership figures), name pronunciation tools, heritage calendars and a Global Culture Party. Only the party reports a figure (over 1,100 employees), and it is a single internal event rather than an ongoing program with measured reach. I was torn between 2 and 3, so I chose the lower level. There is no customer-access or external community-connecting activity. Demographics (E5) are context only.

entrepreneurship.reason: Level 1: the filing shows only the company's own R&D and innovation, with sales aimed at the largest 15,000 companies and no service enabling founders or small businesses.

notes: The Item 7 (targeted) excerpt was empty, so no MD&A paragraphs matched the theme terms. Dynatrace University (online self-service education for customers and partners), Dynatrace Community and customer events were not scored for Community: the filing frames them in Sales and Marketing as nurturing the customer base, which falls under the 'educating customers as marketing' trap. The 'thousands of individuals trained or certified' figure describes GSI partners' own technical readiness investment, not a Dynatrace program, so it was not scored. 'Services the communities that we impact' and 'strengthening belonging' are general language. Operating in about 40 countries and serving customers in over 110 countries does not count for Cross-cultural. The filing refers to a December 2025 Sustainability Report at www.dynatrace.com/company/sustainability/ (main domain), so the Cross-cultural insufficient coverage triggers the second look.
